tb-103-1.question:
Energy is removed from two hot liquids P and Q at the same rate. The two liquids have the same mass and initial temperature. Figure a shows how their temperatures θ vary with time.

Which of the following statements are correct?

(1) The heat capacity of P is larger than that of Q.

(2) The specific heat capacity of P is larger than that of Q.

(3) The average KE of the molecules in P is higher than that in Q at time T.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-103-1.reasoning:
Both liquids lose energy at the same power. Since Q=C|Δθ|, the magnitude of the temperature–time gradient equals power divided by heat capacity. P cools more slowly, so Cₚ>Cᵩ. Their masses are equal, hence C=mc also gives cₚ>cᵩ.

At time T, P has a higher temperature and therefore a higher average molecular kinetic energy. All three statements are correct: D.

tb-103-3.question:
Karen pours water of mass m1 at 90 °C into a cup of water of mass m2 at 20 °C (Fig c). The final temperature of the water is 50 °C. Find m1 : m2.

A 3 : 4

B 4 : 3

C 2 : 9

D 9 : 2
tb-103-3.reasoning:
Energy lost by 90 °C water=energy gained by 20 °C water

m1 × 4200 × (90 − 50) = m2 × 4200 × (50 − 20)

m1 × 40 = m2 × 30

m1m2 = 34

m1 : m2 = 3 : 4

tb-103-4.question:
The set-up below is used to measure the specific heat capacity of a liquid (Fig d).

Which of the following statements correctly describe(s) the function of the apparatus?

(1) The stirrer is used to make the temperature uniform throughout the liquid.

(2) The lid reduces energy loss to the surroundings.

(3) The joulemeter measures the energy supplied to the liquid.

A (1) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-103-4.reasoning:
The stirrer makes the liquid's temperature more uniform, so the thermometer better represents the whole liquid. The lid reduces energy loss, particularly through convection and evaporation.

The joulemeter measures electrical energy supplied to the heater, used to estimate energy supplied to the liquid. A precise analysis also allows for the container and heat losses. Thus all three stated apparatus functions are correct in this experiment: D.

Suppose a larger mass of X is cooled so that its energy is lost at the same rate as before. Which of the following graphs denoted by a dotted line best shows the new relationship between T and t?
tb-103-5.reasoning: A larger mass of X has a higher heat capacity. Therefore, its temperature drops more slowly and the graph should be flatter.

tb-103-6.question:
Figure f shows the variation of the temperature of a liquid with time when the liquid is heated by a 400-W heater. The mass of the liquid is 2 kg. Find the heat capacity of the liquid. Assume all the energy given out by the heater is absorbed by the liquid.

A 600 J °C−1

B 800 J °C−1

C 1200 J °C−1

D 2400 J °C−1
tb-103-6.reasoning:
Energy supplied by heater = energy gained by liquid

Pt = C∆T

400 × (60 − 0) = C × (25 − 15)

C = 2400 J °C−1

tb-103-7.question:
When a metal sphere at a temperature of 100 °C is put into a liquid at a temperature of 20 °C, the final temperature of the liquid is higher than 60 °C. Which of the following must be correct?

A The metal has a higher specific heat capacity than the liquid.

B The sphere has a higher heat capacity than the liquid.

C The sphere has a larger mass than the liquid.

D The energy gained by the liquid is greater than the energy lost by the sphere.
tb-103-7.reasoning: The energy lost by the sphere is equal to the energy gained by the liquid, but the temperature change of the sphere is smaller than the liquid. By C = Q∆T, the sphere has a higher heat capacity than the liquid.

tb-103-8.question:
The specific heat capacity of aluminium is measured using the following set-up (Fig g).

The mass and temperature change of the block are m and ΔT respectively. The energy supplied to the heater as measured by the joulemeter is J. Which of the following is true about the actual specific heat capacity c of the aluminium block? (The energy loss to the surroundings cannot be ignored.)

A c>mJΔT

B c<JmΔT

C c>JmΔT

D c>mJΔT
tb-103-8.reasoning:
As some energy is lost to the surroundings, the energy absorbed by the block Q is smaller than J. Therefore,

c = Qm∆T < Jm∆T

tb-103-10.question:
A 3-kg metal block at 100 °C is put into a 5-kg water bath. The temperature of the water bath rises from 27 °C to 31.7 °C.

(a) State the direction of energy flow. (1 mark)

(b) How does the internal energy of the metal block change? (1 mark)

(c) Find the heat capacity of the metal block. (2 marks)
tb-103-10.answer:
(a) From the metal block to the water 1A

(b) The internal energy of the metal block decreases. 1A

(c) Energy lost by metal block=energy gained by water

C × (100 − 31.7) =5 × 4200 × (31.7 − 27) 1M

C = 1450 J °C−1 1A

tb-103-11.question:
A 1.2-kg hot iron sphere with a heat capacity of 576 J °C−1 is cooled by immersing it fully in a tank of water (Fig i). The mass of the water is 3 kg and its initial temperature is 12 °C. After 5 minutes, both the iron sphere and the water reach a final temperature of 15 °C.

(a) Find the energy gained by the water. (2 marks)

(b) Find the average rate of energy transfer from the iron sphere to the water. (2 marks)

(c) Find the initial temperature of the iron sphere. (2 marks)
tb-103-11.answer:
(a) Q = mc∆T

= 3 × 4200 × (15 − 12) 1M

= 37 800 J 1A

(b) Average rate of energy transfer

= 37 8005×60 1M

= 126 J s−1 1A

(c) Energy lost by iron sphere=energy gained by water

576 × (T − 15) = 37 800 1M

T = 80.6 °C 1A

tb-103-12.question:
(a) State the law of conservation of energy. (1 mark)

(b) A 2-kg steel block at 90 °C and a 5-kg copper block at 70 °C are fully immersed into 9 kg of water at 10 °C. Find the final temperature of the mixture using the law of conservation of energy. Given: specific heat capacity of steel = 450 J kg−1 °C−1 specific heat capacity of copper = 385 J kg−1 °C−1 (2 marks)
tb-103-12.answer:
(a) The total amount of energy in a closed system is conserved, i.e. always kept constant. Energy cannot be created or destroyed. 1A

(b) Energy lost by steel block and copper block=energy gained by water

2 × 450 × (90 − T) + 5 × 385 × (70 − T) =9 × 4200 × (T − 10) 1M

T = 14.6 °C 1A

tb-103-13.question:
Water with initial temperatures of 20 °C and 30 °C flows along water pipe segments X and Y respectively. The water then mixes together in segment Z. The flow rates in X and Y are 5 kg s−1 and 7 kg s−1 respectively (Fig j).

(a) Find the temperature of the water in Z. (2 marks)

(b) With the initial temperatures and flow rates unchanged, the water in the pipe system is replaced by liquid W that has a specific heat capacity of 2500 J kg−1 °C−1. How is the result in (a) affected? (1 mark)
tb-103-13.answer:
(a) In each second,

energy lost by 30 °C water=energy gained by 20 °C water

7 × 4200 × (30 − T) =5 × 4200 × (T − 20) 1M

T = 25.8 °C 1A

(b) The result is not affected. 1A

tb-103-14.question:
An aluminium block of mass 1.6 kg is placed into a well-insulated container (Fig k). An immersion heater and a thermometer are inserted into the holes in the block. A few drops of oil are added to the holes. An energy of 6000 J is supplied to the aluninium block so that its temperature rises from 25 °C to 29 °C.

(a) Calculate the specific heat capacity of aluminium. (2 marks)

(b) After the heater is switched off, the temperature of the block is not recorded immediately. Explain why. (1 mark)

(c) State a source of error in this experiment. Hence, deduce whether the actual value of the specific heat capacity of aluminium would be the same as, higher than, or lower than the experiment result. (3 marks)
tb-103-14.answer:
(a) c = Qm∆T = 60001.6×(29-25) 1M

= 938 J kg−1 °C−1 1A

(b) It takes some time for energy to transfer from the heater to the block. 1A

(c) Some energy is lost to the surroundings. 1A

The energy absorbed by the block is smaller than the energy supplied by the heater. 1A

By c = Qm∆T, the actual value of c of aluminium would be lower than the experiment result. 1A

tb-103-16.question:
Mike puts some fish balls into 800 g of water. The fish-ball-and-water mixture is 20 °C and Mike puts it on a stove to heat it up (Fig m). Take the heat capacity of the fish balls to be 192 J °C−1.

(a) If it takes 5 minutes to heat the mixture up to 90 °C, what is the power of the stove? (3 marks)

(b) He then puts some noodles with a temperature of 15 °C into the water. It takes another 1 minute to heat the mixture up to 90 °C using the same setting. What is the heat capacity of the noodles? (2 marks)
tb-103-16.answer:
(a) Energy supplied by stove=energy gained by mixture

P × (5 × 60) =192 × (90 − 20) + 0.8 × 4200 × (90 − 20) 2M

P = 829 W 1A

(b) Energy supplied by stove =energy gained by noodles

Pt = C∆T

829 × (1 × 60) = C × (90 − 15) 1M

C = 663 J °C−1 1A

tb-103-17.question: Janice is given the following apparatus to measure the specific heat capacity of water c (Fig n). Describe how Janice should conduct the experiment. Write down how she can obtain the value of c by plotting a straight-line graph using data obtained in the experiment. (5 marks)
tb-103-17.answer:
Measure the initial temperature of the water with a thermometer. Set the timer for measuring time. 1A

Turn on the induction cooker to heat the water. Use a stirrer to stir the water thoroughly. 1A

After a certain time t, stop heating and measure the maximum water temperature with the thermometer. Find the change in temperature ∆T. Continue heating to take several sets of data. 1A

Plot a graph of ∆T against t. 1A

The value of c is given by Pm×slope 1A

as ∆T = (Pmc)t.

Suppose 1 kg of water and 1 kg of iron at the same temperature of 20 °C are put in a refrigerator at 4 °C.

(a) Describe and explain the change in the average kinetic energy of the water molecules. (2 marks)

(c) ‘When there is a power failure, the more water inside the refrigerator, the slower the temperature will increase inside the refrigerator.’ Comment on this statement. (3 marks)
tb-103-18.answer:
(a) The average kinetic energy of the water molecules decreases 1A

as the temperature of the water drops.
1A

(b) The specific heat capacity of water is higher than that of iron. 1A

According to Q = mc∆T, the change in the internal energy of the water is larger than that of the iron. 1A

(c) This statement is correct. 1A
